mainTopic: What cancels a כהן's קידוש ידים ורגלים: staying overnight (לינה), leaving the עזרה (יציאה), and becoming טמא (טומאה).
overview: The גמרא first tests the two readings of רבי יוחנן's statement, from אביי and from רבא, against the משנה about כהנים washing in the morning. For אביי the משנה fits רבי. For רבא it seems to fit nobody, until the גמרא explains that it speaks about new כהנים who did not serve that night. Next comes a new question: does leaving the עזרה cancel a כהן's קידוש ידים ורגלים? Several proofs are brought, from hands that went out, from washing outside, from a כהן who left for a moment, and from the פרה אדומה. Each one is pushed aside, so the question about leaving is not settled. Then the גמרא asks a second question: does becoming טמא cancel the washing? It narrows that question to a כהן whose whole body became טמא close to sunset. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a proof from the פרה אדומה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: For אביי, the משנה fits רבי easily
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a challenge with "בשלמא": according to אביי, the משנה matches the view of רבי without any problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for אביי. He reads the statement according to רבי, and he says רבי agrees that between the rooster's crow and morning, staying overnight does not cancel the washing. So the משנה follows רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge by first showing whose view has no problem. Here that is אביי, and next it will show the trouble for רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, רבי holds that לינה cancels the previous day's washing. But רבי agrees that the period from the rooster's crow until morning is not affected by this. So כהנים who served all night could wash again before dawn, and the משנה fits רבי nicely.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for (the first half of a challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not a full answer by itself. The "בשלמא" only means "for this person it works." The real attack comes in the next step with "אלא".

phrases.english: It works well according to Abaye
who explains it according to Rabbi
phrases.notes: "It" is the statement of רבי יוחנן that אביי and רבא disagreed about.

phrases.english: and Rabbi agrees
that from the rooster's crow until morning
staying overnight does not cancel the washing
Whose view is this משנה? It is Rabbi's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a בשלמא/אלא challenge based on the earlier argument between אביי and רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: Setup: shows that אביי has no difficulty with the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It makes a contrast, so the next step can show that רבא has no matching way to explain the משנה.

steps.title: For רבא, the משנה seems to fit nobody
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא, the משנה cannot follow רבי, because the washing would be cancelled at dawn. It also cannot follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, because he says no new washing is needed even for ten days.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about רבא? He reads the statement according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, and he holds that for רבי, staying overnight cancels the washing even between the rooster's crow and morning. So whose view is the משנה? If רבי, the washing gets cancelled anyway. If רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, he said that even for ten days a כהן does not need to wash again!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the real challenge. The גמרא shows that רבא cannot match the משנה to either תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, רבי holds that לינה cancels the washing all the way up to morning, so washing before dawn would be useless. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds that a כהן who keeps serving never needs to wash again. Then why would כהנים who served all night need to wash? Both options fail.

keyTerms.meaning: But (the second half of a challenge)
To wash hands and feet from the כיור

phrases.english: But according to Rava

phrases.aramaic: דְּמוֹקֵים לַהּ כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: who explains it according to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon
but according to Rabbi

phrases.aramaic: מִקְּרוֹת הַגֶּבֶר עַד צַפְרָא פָּסְלָה לִינָה;
phrases.english: from the rooster's crow until morning, staying overnight does cancel it
Whose view is this משנה?
If it is Rabbi, staying overnight cancels it!

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן – הָא אָמַר:
phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, he said:
even from now until ten days
he does not need to wash again!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרָבָא דְּמוֹקֵים לַהּ כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the בשלמא/אלא challenge that began in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's way of explaining רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבא, neither רבי nor רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון can explain why כהנים who served all night wash in the morning.

steps.title: The משנה is about new כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה really follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. It speaks about new כהנים who did not serve during the night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the משנה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. What case are we dealing with here? New כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge for רבא. It changes the case: these כהנים are just starting their service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון only says that a כהן who keeps serving does not need to wash again. כהנים who did not serve that night are starting fresh, so of course they must wash. The משנה fits him after all.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
New כהנים (who did not serve during the night)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבא, the משנה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, and it speaks about new כהנים who are just starting to serve.

phrases.english: Really, it follows Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon
and with what case are we dealing here?
With new priests.
phrases.notes: These are כהנים who did not serve during the night, so they are only starting now.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבא from step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה was about כהנים who served all night.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about new כהנים, so they need to wash even according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

steps.title: Does leaving the עזרה cancel the washing?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: does a כהן's washing get cancelled if he leaves the עזרה? Maybe leaving makes him lose focus. Or maybe it does not, because he can come back whenever he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: does leaving cancel the washing of hands and feet? Suppose you say staying overnight does not cancel it. That may be only because he does not separate from the עזרה. But leaving is a real separation, so maybe he takes his mind off the service. Or perhaps, since he can come back whenever he wants, he does not take his mind off it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a brand-new question about a כהן who leaves the עזרה. It lays out the reasoning for both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question builds on the view that לינה does not cancel washing. One side says leaving is worse than לינה, because he actually separates and loses focus (היסח הדעת). The other side says he does not lose focus, because he can return at any time.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked (a question with no clear answer yet)
Washing hands and feet from the כיור before serving
He takes his mind off it (היסח הדעת)
It is in his power to come back

steps.whyThisMatters: The question shows that the גמרא measures the washing by whether the כהן's focus on the service breaks (היסח הדעת), and not simply by time passing.

phrases.english: They asked:
What about leaving? Does it take effect
phrases.notes: "Take effect" here means cancel the washing, so he would have to wash again.

phrases.english: on the washing of hands and feet?
If you say
staying overnight does not cancel it
that is because he does not separate
but leaving, where he does separate
he surely takes his mind off the service
Or perhaps
since he can come back whenever he wants
he does not take his mind off it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: יְצִיאָה מַהוּ שֶׁתּוֹעִיל בְּקִידּוּשׁ יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question that builds on the idea that לינה does not cancel the washing.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a כהן who leaves the עזרה need to wash his hands and feet again when he comes back?

steps.title: First proof: hands that went out keep their holiness
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if a כהן's washed hands became impure he only needs טבילה, and if they went out they stay holy. This seems to answer the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If a כהן washed his hands and feet and they became impure, he dips them in a מקוה and does not need to wash again. If they went out, they keep their holiness!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question from Step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that if the washed hands 'went out' of the עזרה, they are still holy. So it looks like leaving the עזרה does not cancel the washing. That would settle the question.

keyTerms.meaning: He washed his hands and feet from the כיור before serving
He dips them in a מקוה to make them pure again
In their holiness; the washing still counts

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he washed his hands and feet and they became impure,
he dips them in a מקוה and does not need to wash them again.
If they went out, they keep their holiness!
phrases.notes: "They" means his hands: his washed hands went outside the עזרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question raised in Step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That leaving the עזרה does not cancel the washing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: if the washed hands went out, they keep their holiness.

steps.title: Only hands going out was never the question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא only speaks about the hands going out. The real question is when the כהן's whole body leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: When only his hands went out, we have no question. Our question is when his whole body went out. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by narrowing the question to the case where the whole body leaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry from Step 4 was that leaving makes the כהן lose focus. If only his hands stick out, he is still inside, so he does not lose focus. The ברייתא proves nothing about a כהן who walks out completely.

keyTerms.meaning: We have no question about this
Where we do have a question

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the question was answered. The ברייתא only spoke about hands, so the question about the whole body is still open.

phrases.english: When his hands went out, we have no question;
where we do have a question
is when his whole body went out. What is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצְאוּ יָדָיו לָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לַן, כִּי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 5 by making the question narrower.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the first ברייתא is rejected completely, but the question stays.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא is about hands only, not the whole body leaving.

steps.title: Second proof: washed inside and left, the service is valid
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists ways of washing that invalidate the service, like washing outside. The גמרא infers that someone who washed inside and then left still serves validly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A כהן whose hands and feet are not washed must wash with a כלי שרת inside. If he washed with a כלי שרת outside, or with a regular כלי inside, or dipped in cave water, and then served, his service is invalid. The reason is that he washed outside. But if he washed inside and then went out, his service is valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא and makes a דיוק from it to answer the question about the whole body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא invalidates the service only when the washing itself happened outside. The גמרא reads this to mean that washing inside and then leaving is fine. So leaving, even with the whole body, would not cancel the washing.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy vessels used in the בית המקדש
The reason is X, which shows that without X it would be different (a דיוק)

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: שֶׁלֹּא רָחוּץ יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם –
phrases.english: Come and hear: One whose hands and feet are not washed
washes with a holy vessel inside.
If he washed with a holy vessel outside,
or with a regular vessel inside,
or dipped in cave water, and then served,
his service is invalid.
The reason is that he washed with a holy vessel outside;
but if he washed inside and then went out,
his service is valid!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: שֶׁלֹּא רָחוּץ יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 6 narrowed the question to the whole body, a new source is brought to answer that.
steps.raayaObject: That even when the whole body leaves, the washing is not cancelled.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A דיוק from a ברייתא: only washing outside invalidates, so washing inside and leaving is valid.

steps.title: Maybe 'outside' means only his hands were outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'washed outside' may mean he only stuck his hands out. So the דיוק only covers hands going out, and the whole-body question stays open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps 'washed with a holy vessel outside' means he stuck his hands outside and washed. So when it implies he washed inside and 'went out,' it means he stuck his hand outside, and that is valid. But if his whole body went out, you still have the question.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the second proof by reading the ברייתא as talking only about hands, and leaves the question unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'outside' in the ברייתא means hands stuck out while the body stayed in, then the opposite case is also about hands only. That matches what we already knew in Step 6. Nothing is proven about the whole body leaving.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps; introduces another way to read the source
What is the case? How does it look?

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs only show that hands going out of the עזרה do not cancel the washing. Whether walking out with the whole body cancels it is still an open question.

phrases.english: Perhaps "he washed with a holy vessel outside"
what is the case?
For example, where he stuck his hands outside and washed;
so if he washed inside and "went out,"
meaning he stuck his hand outside,
it is valid.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יָצָא כׇּל גּוּפוֹ תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ.
phrases.english: But if his whole body went out, you still have the question.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא ״קִידֵּשׁ בִּכְלֵי שָׁרֵת בַּחוּץ״ הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the דיוק of Step 7 by explaining the ברייתא's case differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the second ברייתא is rejected; the question about the whole body remains.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's 'outside' may mean only hands were outside, so its opposite case is also only about hands.

steps.title: A ברייתא: even a short exit needs new washing
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד brings a ברייתא to רב פפא: a כהן who left the עזרה for a long time needs טבילה, and one who left for a moment needs קידוש ידים ורגלים. This suggests that leaving does cancel the washing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said to רב פפא: Come and hear. If a כהן went out beyond the wall of the courtyard: if he went out to stay a while, he needs immersion. If he went out just for a moment, he needs to wash his hands and feet again.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד brings a new source to answer the question of whether leaving the עזרה cancels a כהן's washing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that even a short trip outside means the כהן must wash his hands and feet again. That would mean leaving the עזרה does cancel his washing. This would answer the question from step 4: yes, leaving cancels it.

keyTerms.meaning: To stay, to remain there for a while
The כהן's washing of hands and feet from the כיור before the עבודה

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב זְבִיד לְרַב פָּפָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Zevid said to Rav Pappa:
Come and hear:
If he went out beyond the boundary of the wall of the courtyard,
if he went out to stay there, he needs immersion;
if only for a moment,
he needs washing of hands and feet!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב זְבִיד לְרַב פָּפָּא, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proofs in steps 5 and 7 were pushed off, a new ברייתא is brought for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That leaving the עזרה with the whole body cancels the washing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: someone who leaves even for a moment needs קידוש ידים ורגלים again.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about going out to relieve oneself
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the ברייתא is about a כהן who left to relieve himself. That act is what requires new washing, not the leaving itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What case are we dealing with here? Where he went out to relieve himself or to urinate.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes off the proof by saying the ברייתא is talking about a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's ruling comes from what the כהן did outside, which was relieving himself. It does not come from the simple fact that he left. So we still don't know whether just leaving cancels the washing.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? This narrows a source to a specific situation
Literally 'to cover his legs', a polite way to say relieving oneself

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב פפא is arguing with the rule of the ברייתא. He agrees with the rule. He only says the reason for it is relieving oneself, not leaving.

phrases.english: He said to him:
What are we dealing with here?
Where he went out to cover his legs,
phrases.notes: A polite way of saying he went to relieve himself, since people covered their legs with their garment while doing it.

phrases.english: or to urinate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 9 by narrowing the ברייתא's case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The ברייתא does not prove anything about simply leaving.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The washing could be needed because he relieved himself, not because he left.

steps.title: But that rule is already taught clearly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא: another source already says plainly that relieving oneself requires טבילה or washing. Why would this ברייתא say it again?
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is already taught clearly: anyone who relieves himself needs immersion, and anyone who urinates needs washing of hands and feet!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's answer by pointing to a source that already teaches this exact rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא were only about relieving oneself, it would just be repeating a rule that is already stated outright. A source normally doesn't repeat itself for no reason. That suggests the ברייתא is really about plain leaving.

phrases.english: But it is taught explicitly:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in יומא 28a.

phrases.english: Anyone who covers his legs needs immersion,
and anyone who urinates
needs washing of hands and feet!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the דחיה of step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's reading of the ברייתא as being about relieving oneself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading makes the ברייתא repeat a rule that is already stated explicitly.

steps.title: The תנא states the rule and then explains it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the repetition is fine. The תנא gives the rule in general and then explains it in detail.
steps.simpleTranslation: He teaches it, and then goes back and explains it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב פפא by explaining why the rule appears twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying a rule twice is not a problem when the second time explains the first. So רב פפא's reading still stands, and the question about plain leaving stays open.

phrases.english: He teaches it and then explains it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the repetition: a general rule followed by its explanation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא would be pointless if it only repeated the rule about relieving oneself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The repetition is deliberate, so רב פפא's reading holds and the question stays open.

steps.title: Proof from the פרה אדומה
steps.stepSummary: A new proof comes from the פרה אדומה. רבי חייא בר יוסף says the כהן washes inside with a כלי שרת and then goes out. רבי יוחנן says he may even wash outside, with a plain vessel or a clay bowl. This suggests that leaving does not cancel the washing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: about the red heifer, רבי חייא בר יוסף says: he washes with a holy vessel inside, and then goes out. רבי יוחנן says: even outside, even with a regular vessel, even with a clay bowl!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof from the service of the פרה אדומה, which is done outside the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Look at רבי חייא בר יוסף's view. The כהן washes inside and then walks out to do the פרה service. If leaving cancelled the washing, washing inside would be useless. So it seems that leaving the עזרה does not cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: The פרה אדומה (red heifer), whose service is done outside the מקדש
Holy vessels used in the מקדש

phrases.english: Come and hear: the red heifer:
Rabbi Chiya bar Yosef says:
He washes with a holy vessel inside, and goes out.
And Rabbi Yochanan says:
Even outside, and even with a non-holy vessel,
and even with a clay bowl!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof of step 9 was pushed off, a new proof is brought, this time pointing the other way.
steps.raayaObject: That leaving the עזרה does not cancel a כהן's washing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא בר יוסף: the כהן washes inside with a כלי שרת and then goes out to do the פרה service.

steps.title: The red heifer is a special case
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the פרה אדומה proves nothing about the בית המקדש, because all of its work is done outside anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The פרה is different. Since all of its work is done outside, going out does not cancel the washing for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes aside the proof from the פרה אדומה in Step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof said: the כהן may wash and then go out for the פרה, so going out does not cancel washing. רב פפא answers that for the פרה, outside is where the work belongs. So going out there tells us nothing about a כהן who leaves the עזרה during regular service.

keyTerms.meaning: The red heifer, whose ashes purify from contact with the dead

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The red heifer is different,
since all of its acts are done outside,
leaving does not disqualify the washing with regard to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought from the פרה אדומה in Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the פרה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פרה is done outside by nature, so it cannot teach us about leaving the עזרה during regular service.

steps.title: Then why wash at all for the red heifer?
steps.stepSummary: If the פרה is all done outside, why does the כהן need to wash his hands and feet for it at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need him to wash at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's answer from Step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פרה is an outside job, washing seems like a rule that belongs only to the inside service. So why does the כהן wash for the פרה at all?

keyTerms.meaning: Washes hands and feet from the כיור

phrases.english: If so,
why do I need him to sanctify his hands and feet?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's claim that the פרה is an outside service.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the פרה is fully an outside job, the washing rule should not apply to it at all.

steps.title: Washing makes it look like inside service
steps.stepSummary: The כהן washes so that the פרה is done in the same style as the service inside the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is done to be like the service inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of Step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The washing for the פרה is not a full inside rule. It is done to make the פרה look like inside service. Since it is only for the look, leaving does not cancel it, so רב פפא's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to, in the style of

phrases.english: It is to be similar to the service inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the purpose of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Washing for the פרה must mean it is a real inside-style rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The washing is done only to look like inside service, so leaving does not cancel it.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the פרה אדומה is pushed aside. The פרה is done outside, and its washing is only to look like inside service.

steps.title: Does becoming impure cancel the washing?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: if a כהן becomes טמא after washing, does he need to wash again once he is pure?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Does טומאה cancel the washing of hands and feet? Suppose leaving does not cancel it. Maybe that is because the כהן is still fit to serve. Here he is not fit, so maybe he stops paying attention. Or maybe, since he will be fit again, he stays careful and does not stop paying attention.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about טומאה and lays out both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key idea is היסח הדעת, taking one's mind off the service. When a כהן just leaves, he is still fit, so his mind stays on serving. When he becomes טמא he is not fit, so maybe his mind wanders. Or maybe he knows he will be fit again soon, so he stays focused.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
He surely takes his mind off the service

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
Impurity: what is the law, does it work
phrases.notes: "Work" here means work to cancel the washing.

phrases.english: on the sanctification of hands and feet?
If you say
that leaving does not disqualify,
that is because the man is still fit,
but here, where the man is not fit,
he surely takes his mind off;
or perhaps,
since he will become fit again,
he is careful and does not take his mind off?
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording; some versions don't have them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: טוּמְאָה, מַהוּ שֶׁתּוֹעִיל לְקִידּוּשׁ יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the still-unsettled question of step 4. Even supposing leaving does not cancel the washing, it asks whether טומאה is different.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether becoming טמא cancels a כהן's washing, so that he must wash again after becoming pure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the whole topic depends on היסח הדעת, whether the כהן's mind left the service.

steps.title: Proof: impure hands are just immersed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if a כהן's washed hands and feet become טמא, he immerses them and does not need to wash again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If he washed his hands and feet and they became impure, he immerses them and does not need to wash again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question of Step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says טומאה does not cancel the washing. Once the hands are made pure by טבילה, the old washing still counts. That seems to answer the question: טומאה does not cancel washing.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he sanctified his hands and feet and they became impure,
he immerses them,
and he does not need to sanctify them again!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: קִידֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו וְנִטְמְאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question of Step 17 from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: טומאה does not cancel the washing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: washed hands that became impure are immersed, with no need to wash again.

steps.title: The real question is a whole impure body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the question was never about impure hands. It is about a כהן whose whole body became טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We had no question about impure hands. Our question is about when his whole body became impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes aside the proof of Step 18 by narrowing the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When only the hands are impure, the כהן himself is still fit, so his mind stays on serving. The question is about a whole impure body, which makes the כהן himself unfit. The ברייתא does not talk about that case.

keyTerms.meaning: We have no question about it

phrases.english: Where his hands became impure, we have no question;
where we do have a question is when his whole body became impure.
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording; some versions don't have them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 18 by limiting the question to a different case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof only covers impure hands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא is about hands alone, and the question is about the whole body, where the כהן himself is unfit.

steps.title: A whole impure body must wait for sunset
steps.stepSummary: If his whole body is impure, he must wait until sunset to be pure. Surely he loses focus in that time, so why is there any question?
steps.simpleTranslation: His whole body?! Then I can figure it out another way: since he must wait for sunset, he surely takes his mind off the service!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the case from Step 19, saying the answer is obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person whose whole body is טמא must immerse and then wait for הערב שמש before he is fully pure. That long wait would surely make him lose focus. So the washing should obviously be cancelled, and there should be nothing to ask.

keyTerms.meaning: I can figure it out (from a different reason)
Waiting for sunset to become fully pure

phrases.english: His whole body?!
Let me derive it instead:
since he needs to wait for sunset,
he surely takes his mind off!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the narrowed question of Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The question as narrowed in Step 19
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Waiting for sunset is a long break, so the כהן surely loses focus. The answer is obvious, and there is nothing to ask.

steps.title: He became impure close to sunset
steps.stepSummary: The question is about a כהן who became טמא close to sunset, so he does not have a long wait.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where he became impure close to sunset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of Step 20 by making the case very specific.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he became טמא right before sunset, he immerses and is pure almost at once. There is no long wait that would surely break his focus. So the question is real again: does being unfit for a short time make him lose focus?

phrases.english: Such as where he became impure
close to sunset.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A whole impure body always means a long wait for sunset, so the washing is surely cancelled.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is about a כהן who became impure right before sunset, with almost no wait.
steps.whatToRemember: The question is now very exact: a כהן whose whole body became טמא close to sunset. Does being unfit for a short time cancel his washing?

steps.title: A proof attempt from washing for the red heifer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a dispute about the כהן who does the פרה אדומה. רבי חייא בר רבי יוסף says he washes with a כלי שרת inside the Temple and then goes out. רבי יוחנן says he may wash even outside, even with a plain vessel, even with a clay bowl.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear a proof from the case of the red heifer. רבי חייא בר רבי יוסף says: the כהן washes his hands and feet with a Temple vessel inside the Temple, and then he goes out to do the service. רבי יוחנן says: he may wash even outside the Temple, even with a regular vessel, and even with a clay bowl.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to try to answer the question from Step 17. Right now it only quotes the dispute; how it proves anything will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This dispute is about a service done outside the Temple, the burning of the פרה אדומה. According to רבי חייא בר רבי יוסף, the כהן washes inside and then walks out, so there is a gap between the washing and the service. The גמרא will use these details to try to learn something about our question.

keyTerms.meaning: The red heifer, burned to make ashes used for purifying people
Washes his hands and feet before doing a Temple service
Holy vessels used for the Temple service
A clay bowl, a very simple vessel

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the proof is already finished. The גמרא has only quoted the dispute so far. The point it wants to prove is explained on the next amud.

phrases.english: Come and hear: the red heifer –
Rabbi Chiya son of Rabbi Yosef says:
He washes with service vessels inside, and goes out.
And Rabbi Yochanan says: even outside,
and even with a non-holy vessel,
and even with a clay bowl.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 21 narrowed the question to a כהן who became טמא close to sunset. Now the גמרא brings a new source to try to answer that narrowed question.
steps.raayaObject: The open question from Steps 17 and 21: does a כהן who became טמא close to sunset need to wash again once he is pure?
steps.raayaSupportSource: A dispute between רבי חייא בר רבי יוסף and רבי יוחנן about how and where the כהן doing the פרה אדומה washes his hands and feet.
